event_name: Calef's More Wonders of Invisible World published
significance: Robert Calef's More Wonders of the Invisible World (1700) was a Boston merchant's systematic critique of the Salem trials and of Cotton Mather's defense of them, documenting procedural irregularities and attacking the validity of spectral evidence; the work contributed to the reputation revision of the Salem proceedings in the eighteenth century and represents a lay voice challenging clerical authority over witchcraft prosecution.
source_method: Published primary source (London, 1700); analyzed in Boyer and Nissenbaum, Salem Possessed (1974) and Norton, In the Devil's Snare (2002)
